h1: The 8 Best Wet-Dry Vacuums for Carpet Spills and Floods, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Wet-Dry Vacuums for Carpet: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 wet-dry vacuums for carpet scored on tank size, motor rating, hose reach, filters and price, from 1.5 to 9 gallons.
summary: The DEWALT 9 Gallon DXV09PA is the wet-dry vacuum to buy for recurring carpet spills, with a large tank, a blower port and a full attachment kit. The DEWALT 6 Gallon DXV06P is the better size for most homes, the Stanley SL18116P is the strongest value under $50, and the Armor All AA155 is the cheap first shop vac for small accidents.
intro: Most people shop for horsepower and regret it. A peak HP number on a wet-dry vacuum is a motor rating taken at the instant of startup, not a measure of how much water the machine pulls out of a rug, and nearly every model in this price range prints a number between 2 and 5. What actually decides whether your carpet dries or turns into a swamp is tank size, nozzle choice and how the filter is set up for liquids.

So this ranking sorts by capacity, practicality and wet-pickup readiness instead of the biggest number on the box. We reviewed eight shop vacuums from their listings and spec sheets, covering tank volume, stated motor rating, bundled attachments, blower function and filter design. Where a listing does not state a detail, we leave it out rather than guess.

products.name: DEWALT 9 Gallon Wet/Dry VAC, Heavy-Duty Shop Vacuum with Attachments, 5 Peak HP, with Blower Function, DXV09PA
products.verdict: A nine-gallon tank, a 5 peak HP motor, a blower port and a real attachment kit.
products.description:
The DXV09PA is the roomiest machine in this ranking, with a 9 gallon tank, a 5 peak HP motor and a blower function. It ships with attachments, which matters on carpet because the bare hose end is the wrong tool for pulling water out of pile.

It takes the top spot because capacity is the quiet limiter on a wet cleanup. A cup of spilled coffee fits in anything, but a leaking water heater or a flooded laundry room can fill a 4 gallon drum in minutes, and every trip to the drain is a pause while the carpet keeps wicking moisture downward. The blower port also doubles as a way to push air across a damp patch afterward. The tradeoff is size: a 9 gallon poly drum is bulky to store and the only pick here in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Buy it if your home has recurring spills, a basement that sometimes takes water or a garage you also want to clean. Skip it if the vacuum has to live in a hall closet.
pros: Nine gallon tank limits emptying trips
Blower function helps dry damp spots
cons: Bulky drum is hard to store
Most expensive pick in the ranking
products.idealFor: Households with recurring spills or a damp basement.
products.skipIf: You only need to clear small spills now and then.

products.name: DEWALT Shop Vacuum 6 Gal 4 HP Poly Wet/Dry Vacuum with Blower DXV06P
products.verdict: A six-gallon poly tank with a blower port, sized for a closet instead of a garage.
products.description:
The DXV06P is a 6 gallon poly-tank wet-dry vacuum rated at 4 peak HP, with a blower function. Poly means a molded plastic drum that will not rust or dent, which is a practical edge when the tank sits wet between uses.

It ranks just under the 9 gallon model because the smaller drum is the only real difference in what it does. Six gallons is enough for most carpet accidents: a spilled mop bucket, a pet mess, a washer hose that slipped off. What you lose is headroom for a true flood, and you also give up the larger machine's bundled attachment emphasis. In return it is easier to carry and costs less, landing in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It is the safest recommendation for a typical house. The caveat is that you will need to empty it more often during a big job.
pros: Rust-proof poly tank holds six gallons
Easier to carry than nine gallons
cons: Fills quickly in a real flood
products.idealFor: Typical homes that want one capable all-round shop vac.
products.skipIf: You expect to clear standing water often.

products.name: Stanley - SL18116P Wet/Dry Vacuum, 6 Gallon, 4 Horsepower Black
products.verdict: Six gallons and a 4 horsepower rating at the lowest price tier for a tank this size.
products.description:
The Stanley SL18116P pairs a 6 gallon tank with a 4 horsepower rating in the $25 to $50 bracket. That puts it level with the DEWALT DXV06P on paper while undercutting it on price.

It lands third because it is the budget way to get the same volume. The gap is in details a spec line cannot show: build quality of the latch and wheels, how the hose locks in, and how long the plastic holds up when it is dragged across a garage floor. DEWALT's reputation in the tool aisle is the reason it ranks above. For occasional carpet cleanup, though, the extra cost buys little you will notice.

Pick it if you want a big tank for the least money and will not run it daily. Skip it if you expect to use it every week for hours.
pros: Six gallons at a budget price
Good first shop vac for carpet
cons: Build feels basic next to DEWALT
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want capacity for the least money.
products.skipIf: You want a blower port or heavy daily use.

products.name: DEWALT DXV04T 4 Gallon 5 Peak HP Portable Corded Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A portable four-gallon DEWALT with the same 5 peak HP rating as the big drum.
products.description:
The DXV04T is a 4 gallon portable corded vacuum with a 5 peak HP motor. It is the smallest DEWALT in this ranking and the easiest to lift one-handed up a flight of stairs.

It ranks fourth because the tank is the limit. Four gallons will handle a spilled drink, a tipped plant or a pet accident without trouble, but it fills quickly if you are pulling water off a large patch of pile. The motor rating is the same as the 9 gallon model, which tells you how little peak HP separates these machines and how much the drum matters. It beats the Vacmaster on portability and the cheaper brands on build.

It suits apartments and large carpeted areas that need frequent light cleanups. The caveat is that long jobs mean frequent emptying.
cons: Costs more than similar small tanks
products.idealFor: Apartment dwellers and light, frequent carpet cleanups.
products.skipIf: Your spills tend to be gallons, not cups.

products.name: Vacmaster Professional VDK811PW 0201 8 Gal Wet/Dry Vac Self-Cleaning Filter
products.verdict: An eight-gallon tank with a self-cleaning filter, aimed at dusty work as much as spills.
products.description:
The Vacmaster VDK811PW has an 8 gallon tank and a self-cleaning filter system. That filter feature is its identity: it is meant to shake loose or clear debris so suction does not fade as dust builds up.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives little beyond tank size and the filter claim, so we cannot credit it for hose length, attachments or motor rating. Self-cleaning is useful when you switch between dry debris and damp pickup, since clogged filters are the usual reason a shop vac loses pull. Against the DEWALT 9 gallon it gives up brand backing and a blower port, but it sits in the same $50 to $100 bracket as the smaller DEWALT units while offering more volume.

Buy it if you vacuum dust and drywall dirt as often as water. Skip it if you want documented attachments.
pros: Eight gallons for a mid price
products.idealFor: Mixed jobs that alternate between dust and water.
products.skipIf: You want a proven attachment kit included.

products.name: Amazon Basics Wet Dry Shop Vacuum Cleaner, 4 Gallon, 3 HP Stainless Steel, Grey/Black
products.verdict: A stainless-steel four-gallon tank rated at 3 HP, sized for smaller rooms.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics shop vacuum has a 4 gallon stainless steel tank and a 3 HP rating. Steel does not crack or warp, and it is easy to rinse out after a messy job.

It places sixth because the motor rating trails the DEWALT units, and its role is narrower: smaller rooms and quick cleanups. Stainless also adds weight and can dent a floor when dropped, which the poly drums avoid. Against the Stanley it gives you a sturdier tank for the same general job but a smaller one, and it costs more, sitting in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It is a fair choice for a studio or a bedroom with a pet. Skip it if you want the largest tank for the money.
pros: Suits smaller rooms and quick jobs
cons: Costs more than Stanley per gallon
products.idealFor: Small homes that value an easy-to-clean steel tank.
products.skipIf: You want the most capacity for the money.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 2.5 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Wet Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A 2.5 gallon, 2.5 peak HP CRAFTSMAN for tight storage and small messes.
products.description:
The CMXEVBE17250 is a 2.5 gallon vacuum with a 2.5 peak HP rating in the $25 to $50 bracket. It is a small, light machine meant for cars, workbenches and spills of a pint or two.

It ranks seventh because the tank is too small for serious carpet work. Wet pickup fills 2.5 gallons in a few passes, and the lower motor rating limits how much liquid it will draw from a thick pad. It still beats the Armor All on size and rating, and it carries a better-known name. Its strength is that it stores almost anywhere.

It is a sensible second vacuum for the car or a shelf in the garage. Skip it as your only machine if you have kids, pets or a basement.
pros: Low price for a known brand
Light enough to move with one hand
products.idealFor: A second vacuum for cars, benches and small spills.
products.skipIf: It will be your only wet-dry vacuum.

products.name: Armor All® AA155 1.5-Gallon 2 Peak HP Portable Wet/Dry Vacuum, Orange
products.verdict: The smallest and cheapest option here, a 1.5 gallon portable for first-time buyers.
products.description:
Armor All's AA155 is the pocket-sized option here: an orange portable unit holding 1.5 gallons, driven by a 2 peak HP motor. It sits at the bottom of the $25 to $50 bracket in every sense, from capacity to power.

It ranks last because 1.5 gallons is closer to a large bucket than a shop vac. It will take a spilled glass or a muddy footprint, and it is the easiest unit here to carry and store. It will not clear a flooded patch of carpet without constant emptying, and its low motor rating means thicker rug pad stays damp. Against the CRAFTSMAN it gives up capacity and brand weight for a lower starting cost.

It makes sense as a first purchase or a car vacuum. Skip it for anything larger than a bathmat.
pros: Light enough for stairs and cars
cons: Lowest motor rating in the group
products.idealFor: First-time buyers with small, occasional messes.
products.skipIf: You may face real water on carpet.

whatMatters.detail: A wet-dry vacuum stores everything it pulls up, so the drum fills long before the motor tires. A 4 gallon tank is ample for a spill but empties often in a flood, while 8 and 9 gallon tanks let a single pass finish. Read the gallon figure on the listing and match it to your worst realistic accident, not your average one.

Peak horsepower is the maximum the motor reaches at startup, not the power it holds while running. That is why a 2 peak HP and a 5 peak HP machine can look closer in real use than the numbers suggest. Treat it as a tier marker, and put more weight on tank size, hose design and filter setup.

Paper dry-pickup filters swell and tear when wet, so most manufacturers want a foam sleeve or no cartridge filter at all during liquid work. Check the manual or listing for wet-use guidance. A self-cleaning filter, as on the Vacmaster, helps when you switch between dry and damp debris.

Carpet needs a wide squeegee or floor nozzle to lift moisture from pile, and the bare hose end only works for puddles on hard surfaces. Look for an attachment kit in the listing, as on the DEWALT 9 gallon. A missing nozzle is a small extra purchase but an easy one to forget.

Several models list a blower function, which pushes air out of the exhaust to move leaves or dry a damp area. It does not replace a dehumidifier, but it speeds surface drying after extraction. Both DEWALT six and nine gallon models list it in this ranking.

faq.q: Can a wet-dry vacuum replace a carpet cleaner?
faq.a: Not for deep cleaning. A shop vac only extracts liquid and does not spray solution or scrub fibers, so it is the right tool for a flood or a spill, not for removing ground-in dirt. For routine cleaning you would still use a carpet cleaner.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with these machines?
faq.a: Leaving the dry paper filter in place for liquid pickup. A wet paper filter tears and clogs, and some manuals tell you to remove it entirely or use a foam sleeve. Check the guidance for your model before the first spill.

faq.q: Is the 9 gallon DEWALT worth it over the 6 gallon?
faq.a: If you expect real water, yes, since fewer trips to the drain keep the carpet from soaking further. For ordinary spills the 6 gallon DXV06P does the same work and is easier to store.

faq.q: How do I set one up for water?
faq.a: Remove or swap the dry filter as the manual directs, attach a floor or squeegee nozzle, and make sure the tank is empty. Plug into a grounded outlet away from standing water, and run the nozzle slowly in overlapping strokes.

faq.q: How should I clean and store the tank?
faq.a: Empty it after every wet job and rinse the drum with a hose. Let it air-dry with the lid off so mildew does not build up. A stainless tank like the Amazon Basics is the easiest to wipe out.

faq.q: Does a higher peak HP number mean more suction?
faq.a: Only loosely. Peak HP is a startup rating, so a 5 peak HP unit and a 4 HP unit may feel similar in use. Hose size, filter condition and tank fullness shape suction more than that label.

finalTake: For carpets that actually get wet, the DEWALT 9 Gallon DXV09PA is the best wet-dry vacuum here, with its large tank, blower port and attachments. The DEWALT DXV06P is the right size for most houses, and the Stanley SL18116P gives you six gallons for the lowest outlay. Keep the CRAFTSMAN or Armor All for cars and small spills. Match the tank to your worst-case accident and ignore the horsepower headline.
